title: State v. Earls (N.J. 2013)
key_points: Holding: Under the NJ Constitution, police need a warrant (or an exception such as exigency) to obtain cell phone location information from a provider.
officer_notes: Scenario: Looking for a burglary suspect, you ask the carrier to ping his phone without a warrant or emergency.
Takeaway: Location data requires a warrant unless a real emergency exists.
